title: Did Italy's Leader Really 'Beg' for a Photo? A Big Fight with Trump
summary: Have you ever been accused of something you didn't do? That's how Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni feels. She says U.S. President Donald Trump told a made-up story about her. Trump claimed that Meloni "begged" him to take a picture with her at a big meeting in France. He said, "She begged me to take a picture with her. She wanted a picture with me so badly. I wouldn't have taken it, but I felt sorry for her." But Meloni says that's not true at all. She posted a video saying Trump's words are "completely fabricated"—which means totally made up. "I am frankly stunned," she said. "I don't know why the president of the United States behaves this way toward his own allies." Meloni used to be one of Trump's biggest supporters in Europe. She visited him after he won the 2024 election and went to his inauguration. But they've disagreed on many things lately, like the war in Ukraine and Trump's threats to take over Greenland. In her video, Meloni said it was a "shame" Trump doesn't show the same toughness toward enemies as he does toward her. "Italy and I do not beg," she said firmly. Right after her video, Italy's foreign minister canceled his trip to the U.S. He was supposed to meet with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Other Italian leaders also spoke up. The justice minister said Trump's words hurt the memory of American soldiers who died freeing Italy in World War II. The defense minister said he doesn't believe Meloni would ever beg, "not even under threat." The White House hasn't answered Meloni's comments yet. For now, this fight between two countries that are supposed to be friends is getting bigger.
why_it_matters: It's important to tell the truth and stand up for yourself when someone says something false about you, even if that person is powerful.

background_read: Italy and the United States have been close allies since World War II, when American soldiers helped free the country from dictatorship.
Giorgia Meloni (Italy's first female prime minister, in office since 2022) was once a strong supporter of Donald Trump (the U.S. president, re-elected in 2024).
When world leaders meet, official photos show friendship and cooperation, so a false story about begging can cause a serious diplomatic argument.
Article_Structure: WHO: Giorgia Meloni, Italy's prime minister, and Donald Trump, the president of the United States.
WHAT: Trump claimed Meloni begged for a photo, but Meloni says that never happened — she called his words 'completely fabricated' and said she was 'stunned'.
WHERE: The alleged incident happened at a meeting in France; the diplomatic fight now involves Italy and the U.S.
WHY: Meloni and Italy feel insulted and want to defend their dignity; this public clash is straining a long-time friendship between the two countries.

perspectives.description: Giorgia Meloni showed courage by publicly correcting a false story from a powerful U.S. president, defending her country's pride and respect.
Critics worry that Donald Trump's behavior could damage the trust and cooperation between the United States and its old friend Italy.
Some observers note that Trump has often been tough on allies while being less confrontational with countries like Russia, raising questions about his foreign policy strategy.
